data.narrative:
Deep Fission, a nuclear energy company founded by Liz Muller and Rich Muller, is preparing for IPO following $80M in total capital raised. The valuation universe comprises 9 peers across the nuclear energy sector: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 6 private firms including X-Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and Nano Nuclear Energy.

Peer-median methodology was not applicable in this instance. The nuclear energy sector contains only one same-stage peer and zero adjacent-stage or comparable-tier private comparables, falling short of the three-datapoint minimum required for reliable median derivation. Expanding to all-sector peers would introduce substantial methodological noise given the heterogeneity of capital intensity, development timelines, and regulatory pathways across nuclear subsegments. The public market comps (OKLO, NNE, SMR) offer limited guidance; these represent post-IPO valuations that may not reflect pre-listing multiples or Deep Fission's specific capital position.

This analysis cannot support a specific valuation range based on quantitative triangulation. The narrow peer cohort, combined with limited transparency into private comparables' recent funding rounds and post-money valuations, prevents reliable multiple-based anchoring. A defensible valuation would require either (1) access to recent funding multiples from the five named private peers, or (2) fundamental modeling tied to Deep Fission's specific asset base, regulatory pathway, and cash burn profile—neither of which is available in the current dataset.
